title: The stairwell door at North Stack Night School

grounding:
## Technology
- **emTech:** ai
- **Product category:** Open-weight, edge-runnable language assistants — tutoring, drafting, translation and quizzing software that runs on hardware a community controls (locked laptops, phones, a mini PC under the table), offline or on a room-only link.

## Capabilities
Explain a stuck exam step, draft and check a form, translate plain-language rights material, and quiz a learner in natural language — on-device, with no prompt sent to a distant server. Quality is below the largest cloud systems but adequate for certificate-track tutoring and form help when the workflow around it exists.

## Trends & predictions
Open-weight releases through 2025–2026 (including efficient sparse tiers that activate only a slice of their weights per token, and smaller distilled models), quantization, and mature local runtimes keep pushing useful assistance onto cheaper hardware. **Forecast (not lock):** offline tutoring on secondhand laptops becomes routine where power, storage, and a safe update path hold; legal and exam accuracy still lag and need human gates.

## Milestone
Around 2026, capable open-weight models plus local runtimes make private, offline classroom assistance realistic on hardware a night school can own — the strong versions no longer live only behind cloud APIs that log every sentence.

## Honest limits
Confident wrong answers on legal or exam content are worse than a slow human; keep human review on those. Volunteers can learn a runbook, not run a model-ops team. Building power and secondhand hardware fail. A loud "private lab" brand makes the stairwell lock pointless — design for ordinary cover. One room, one certificate track, or one device cart first; not a national underground network in 2026.

## Unlocks Use Case(s)
Room-only tutoring that never crosses a monitored gateway; form and rights help with custody of the learner's words; low-signature study tools that look like ordinary night-school kit.

## Applications
Shared device carts with a volunteer runbook; offline exam-prep assistants with syllabus-checked answer gates; room-network study helpers with explicit, rare, stripable sync for updates; first-session flows that let a nervous learner start without feeling watched. Invent the local system — kit, keys, update path, human gates.

mission.briefMd:
## The place

Omar locks the stairwell door before he powers the secondhand laptop. The bulb in the North Stack corridor hums. On the third floor of the block, twelve adults unfold cheap chairs around two folding tables. This is night school: exam prep, job forms, and the plain language of rights that the daytime curriculum skips.

He opens the study page the city library still recommends. It spins. Then it dies mid-sentence on a history question. The public filter won again.

Last month someone typed a careful question about assembly law into the free help on the shared account. The session froze. Two days later a block warden asked why the community room was studying politics. Three learners stopped coming. They still need the certificate. They will not risk another flag.

Omar prints worksheets while the toner lasts and answers what he can from memory. The queue is longer than one volunteer. Learners who can pay for private tutors leave the stack. Everyone else learns to ask smaller questions.

## The bigger problem

North Stack is one room in a country where learning runs through pipes someone else watches. Every useful study tool gets useful by sending each question out of the building, where it can be throttled, logged, or turned into a knock on the door.

The root is not a lack of curiosity, and not a missing gadget. It is a system that decides who may read what, and that makes convenience point at the watcher. Fear teaches silence faster than any lesson plan. When the room goes quiet, funders read it as low demand, and the volunteers who kept it open burn out first.

## Your job

Invent a way these adults can get real help with exams, forms, and their rights without one word of it leaving this room, on nights when the building power and the connection both fail. Stakeholder: **Omar, volunteer tutor lead**, who faces the learners after every outage and every rumor of a flagged account, and will not deploy anything that gets someone hurt.

suggestedWhy.ai: A tutor that runs on the school's own laptops, offline, can lift Learning without sending a learner's words away.
suggestedWhy.computing: A cheap box under the table that holds the help locally keeps questions in the room, so Fear has less to feed on.
suggestedWhy.networks: A room-only link between the devices lets one runbook serve twelve learners, easing Burnout for the volunteers.
